blocks.content: The legal framework provides the structural foundation for regulatory oversight, ensuring financial stability and institutional integrity.

rows: Derived directly from specific articles in the Constitution of India
Created by an Act passed by Parliament or State Legislature
Requires a Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368
Requires an amendment law enacted by a simple legislative process
Reserve Bank of India (RBI Act 1934), SEBI (SEBI Act 1992)

items: Competitive exams frequently test the exact division of power: RBI Act, 1934 governs monetary policy functions, whereas Banking Regulation Act, 1949 governs bank licensing and operational control.
Remember the exact date of RBI nationalization: January 1, 1949.
Be prepared to distinguish between Constitutional Bodies (e.g., CAG, Finance Commission) and Statutory Bodies (e.g., RBI, SEBI).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, under the statutory provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Initially established in Kolkata, the central office of the RBI was permanently relocated to Mumbai in 1937.
The institution was nationalized on January 1, 1949, through the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provides the core legal framework empowering regulatory oversight, licensing, and management supervision over commercial banks.
